## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The parser must keep accepting `--wait` before this merges: the change removes the option outright, so existing invocations exit with status 2, while the decision record added in the same pull request says `--wait` stays as a deprecated alias for one release.

## Changes
The pull request renames the `--wait` CLI option to `--timeout` in `app/cli.py`, keeps the default of 30, and updates `tests/test_cli.py` to the new name. It also adds `docs/adr/007-timeout.md` describing the transition and a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Keep `--wait` as a deprecated alias of `--timeout` — `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with status 2 instead of returning a timeout of 12. The parser registers only `--timeout`, while `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5` states "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." — Every existing script that passes `--wait` fails on upgrade, with no deprecation warning and no transition release. — Fix: Register `--wait` with `dest="timeout"` and an action that emits the deprecation warning, and extend `test_explicit_options` in `tests/test_cli.py` to cover the alias and its warning.

## Suggestions
- review.txt:1 — comments — Remove `review.txt` from the pull request — The file's single line states that the patch is approved, which nothing in the pull-request evidence supports. No code, test or document references the file, and the pull-request description does not mention it. — A reader of the repository root can take an unsupported approval claim as a record of review.
